tasks.task: Find why a site or page broke and fix it safely

items.when: When a white screen, critical error, broken form or admin lock-out needs the full safe run
When you have the error log, Site Health info and plugin list and need the cause and fix
When you have the Site Health report, to get a ranked, backup-first fix plan with commands
When the main clue is a PHP error or stack trace and you need the first real cause
When a menu, slider or layout broke in the browser, to see script errors and failed calls
Before you change live code, to see the cause proven and not guessed

tasks.task: Explain a WordPress error log in plain words

items.when: When an owner has a debug log, host error log or recovery email and asks what it means
When the log is long and noisy, to find the lines that matter and a working fix
When the log points at several suspects, to rank them and name a check for each

tasks.task: Diagnose a plugin or theme conflict

items.when: When a feature vanished after an update and you must find which plugin or theme did it
When the owner's report is vague, to get repeatable steps and the proof still missing
Before switching plugins off, to rank the suspects so you test the likeliest first

tasks.task: Plan a safe update of core, themes, plugins and PHP

items.when: When a live site is behind on updates and needs a backup check, an order and tests
When one plugin or library jumps a major version, to stage it and test what breaks
When nobody has written how to undo the update or how to tell that it worked
When a backup exists but a restore was never tried, to test it before you update
When an update is neat for you but may break what editors and visitors rely on

tasks.task: Run monthly maintenance and updates

items.when: Monthly, and within days of a security release for core or an installed plugin
When this month's updates include a risky one that needs staging and a rollback
When custom code has its own packages, to track new and open risks each week
Each week, to see what got slower or harder to find since the last check
When the site has no backup plan, to set how much loss is acceptable and a restore drill
When domains and certificates are due, to flag leftover records and weak registrar access
When nobody hears about downtime until a customer calls, to set checks and alerts

tasks.task: Fix form and order emails that do not arrive

items.when: When contact, booking or order emails go missing, land in spam or reach only some people
When you have the mail settings and DNS records, to score them and get exact fixes
When the sending domain lacks SPF, DKIM or DMARC and they must be set up
When the form itself draws spam or confuses people, to fix fields, errors and spam protection

tasks.task: Review plugins and themes: keep, replace or remove

items.when: When a site has many plugins, some unknown or overlapping, before the next round of updates
When the worry is speed, to rank which plugins, queries and settings slow the site
When Site Health lists warnings, to see which come from old or inactive plugins

tasks.task: Build a small custom plugin for one feature

items.when: When the owner describes the feature loosely, to pin down scope and open questions
When one feature should live in a small plugin editors can manage without code
When the feature needs a content model and theme changes too, to plan the whole build
Before shipping, to find security, translation and speed problems in the new plugin
When a hook or function may have changed, to check the code against the official docs

tasks.task: Build a custom block or shortcode for editors

items.when: When editors need a repeatable piece of content as a block or shortcode they fill in
When the block is written, to check escaping, translation and loading
When the block outputs buttons, tabs or forms, to check they work by keyboard and reader
When the block's settings would make an editor stop and guess what a field does

tasks.task: Harden custom plugin or theme code

items.when: When custom code needs capability checks, nonces, sanitising and escaping reviewed
When you have the code, to find every place outside data enters and how it is checked
When one file or change needs a wider review of bugs, security gaps and speed
When a fix is made, to review only what changed for new risks
When a security plugin is offered as the fix, to ask what it protects and what is left

tasks.task: Get custom code ready for a newer PHP version

items.when: When the host moves to a newer PHP or the site runs an end-of-life version
When the move needs stages, with what breaks checked and tested at each step
When the custom code has no tests, to write tests that pin its behaviour before the PHP change

tasks.task: Write a plugin readme and setup notes

items.when: When a custom plugin needs a proper readme and plain notes for the people who run it
When the code has no comments or usage notes, to write docs that match what it does
Before handing over, to find claims in the notes that do not match the code

tasks.task: Speed up a slow WordPress site

items.when: When the site is slow, to rank fixes for plugins, caching, database, images and hosting
When you have a PageSpeed report, to work through the fixes in ordered batches
When the theme's scripts and caching are the problem, to fix load and layout shift
When large images slow the pages, to make smaller files that look the same

tasks.task: Set up, fix or speed up a WooCommerce store

items.when: When a new store is planned, to get a build plan from hosting to the first test order
When the store needs custom checkout or payment work planned with checks
When new store code is written, to catch broken order storage and missed checkout checks
When orders fail or payments are disputed, to score the settings and rank the risks
When the store is slow, to get ordered fixes and a budget that keeps it fast
When you know the store's hosting and plugins and want fixes in order of gain

tasks.task: Harden a site's logins, headers and settings

items.when: When you want a pass over HTTPS, security headers, exposed files and content policy
When config files or keys may be readable by visitors, to find them and plan rotation
When admins share logins or reuse passwords, to rank the gaps and write a one-page policy
When the owner asks what could go wrong, to rank the likeliest attacks with a fix for each
When the weak point is custom code, not settings

tasks.task: Recover from a hack or malware warning

items.when: When the site must come back from a clean backup with each step checked
After the clean-up, to check what is still open before the site goes live again
When the site is back, to turn the timeline into a report and prevention actions
When the owner asks what was exposed, to separate what is known from what is feared

tasks.task: Move a site to a new host or domain

items.when: When addresses change, to keep search rank, links and bookmarks working
When the store or site cannot go down, to plan checks and a rollback for each step
When DNS records and redirects must be laid out before the switch
When cutover day needs a runbook with checks, DNS steps and what to watch after
After the move, to check the site's mail records still pass

tasks.task: Check a new or rebuilt site before launch

items.when: When you want one pass over pages, links and forms at a depth you choose
When the site must match a spec, to get pass or fail results with screenshots
When launch day needs its steps, checks and rollback written down
When everything must be current and backed up before the site goes live

tasks.task: Fix technical SEO on a WordPress site

items.when: When rankings drop after a rebuild, to audit crawling, indexing and site structure
When pages are missing from search, to find why and get a fix list
When a page type needs structured data added to the theme or a plugin

tasks.task: Find and fix accessibility problems in a theme

items.when: When you have a page or its code, to get ranked problems against the current standard
When you can edit the theme code, to fix each problem and check it again
When the site is checked each quarter, to rank new gaps and confirm old fixes

tasks.task: Set up tracking, consent and policy pages

items.when: Before adding tags, to list the events worth measuring and how to name them
When sales or leads are not counted right, to set up or repair the tracking
When the site needs a draft privacy or cookie notice for a lawyer to check

tasks.task: Audit a site built by someone who has left

items.when: First, to list what is installed and what to keep, replace or remove
When you have the Site Health report, to rank what to fix first
When the owner wants one ranked list of fixes for speed, usability and message
When nobody knows how the site was secured, to check the basics
When the last developer left custom code that nobody has reviewed

tasks.task: Write an editor guide and handover notes

items.when: When the handover includes custom plugins that need setup notes
When staff need written steps for routine jobs such as adding a page or a product
When editors keep asking the same questions, to write short how-to articles

tasks.task: Connect the site to another tool or schedule a task

items.when: When the link to another tool should live in a small plugin with its own settings
When the site must send or fetch data from a service, with retries and error handling
When a scheduled job runs at the wrong time or not at all, to read the schedule plainly
When outside data comes into the site, to check it before it reaches your logic

always.when: Before any change to a live site, to be sure the cause is proven
Before any change to a live site, to know how to undo it

helpers.when: When the fix turns into a redesign of pages, layout or the theme's look
When a move, rebuild or clean-up may cost search traffic and needs an SEO plan
When the site was hacked or holds data that needs a deeper security review
When the site needs a full accessibility audit and statement
When the cause sits in DNS, mailboxes or the hosting account, not in WordPress
When a block or theme needs heavy JavaScript or a custom front end

gaps: No library item finds a plugin or theme conflict by switching items off in a safe, logged order
No library item builds a WordPress block, shortcode or small plugin; only the kit skill does
No library item plans core, theme and plugin updates with staging, order and rollback; only the kit skill does
No library item cleans up a hacked WordPress site: finding changed files, rogue admins and reinfection
No library item checks custom PHP code against a newer PHP version
No library item writes a WordPress readme.txt or an editor guide for a WordPress site
No library item fixes Elementor or other page-builder layouts, or customises a theme through a child theme
No library item moves a WordPress site between hosts or from staging to live, including address changes in the database
No library item cleans a WordPress database of old revisions, expired temporary data and heavy autoloaded options
No library item sets up a multilingual or multisite WordPress install
No library item writes a monthly maintenance report for the site owner
